articles.title: Fantasy Football Matchups to Exploit: Look to Panthers-Browns for points in Week 3
articles.summary: Ray Garvin goes through players in the best spots to succeed in Week 3 for your fantasy football lineups.
articles.body:
Two weeks into the NFL season, defensive rankings are starting to look useful. They can also get you into trouble.

We are still dealing with small samples. One bad game can make a defense look like a matchup we need to attack every week, while one slow performance can hide an issue that becomes much more obvious over time. So when I am looking for matchups to exploit this early in the season, I want to start with the player first.

Give me the role. Give me the usage. Give me something happening within the offense that I already believe in. Then we can use the opponent to figure out where it makes sense to get more aggressive than consensus.

Here are five spots I want to attack in Week 3.

Bryce Young has been on an absolute heater to start the season.

You can say whatever you want about the opponents, but Young can play only the teams on his schedule. Through two games, he has completed 46-of-73 passes for 648 yards, six touchdowns and one interception. He threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns against Chicago, then followed it up with 287 yards and three more scores against Atlanta.

More important than the box score is how different this Brad Idzik-led Carolina offense looks. Young is playing with confidence. The offense feels tailored to what he does well and Carolina is giving him opportunities to push the ball through the air instead of asking him to survive every dropback.

The Browns have allowed 19.0 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through two weeks and 0.151 EPA per opponent dropback across 64 dropbacks. Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdowns against them in Week 1.

This will not be easy on the road, especially with Carolina sitting as a 2.5-point favorite in a game with a modest 41.5-point total. Still, Young has legitimate weapons on the outside and another big red-zone target in Darren Waller. I think the pieces are there for his strong play to continue.

I have Young as my QB13 compared to QB16 in Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR). My projection is actually much more conservative than what he has produced so far, with 213 passing yards, 1.7 passing touchdowns, 14 rushing yards and 16.5 fantasy points. His simulation ceiling sits at 26 points.

If you are looking outside the obvious top-10 quarterbacks this week, Young is one of my favorite streaming options.

A lot of fantasy managers entered the season worried about Jonathon Brooks taking work away from Chuba Hubbard.

Two games in, Hubbard just keeps producing.

He has 22 carries for 102 yards and a touchdown, but what has really stood out has been his work in the receiving game. Hubbard has caught all five of his targets for 49 yards and two touchdowns. Young is looking for him as a receiver and that type of usage gives Hubbard another path to fantasy production beyond simply grinding out carries.

He also led Brooks in touches again in Week 2 before Brooks exited with a groin issue.

We saw Bucky Irving have success against Cleveland and while Jacksonville did not need to lean heavily on its running game, the underlying numbers still create an interesting spot for Carolina. Cleveland has allowed 0.063 EPA per rush and a 50.0 percent rushing success rate on 54 qualifying opponent rushes.

That is where the combination gets interesting to me. Hubbard has the lead role, he is getting scoring opportunities and his quarterback is involving him in the passing game.

I have Hubbard ranked as my RB9 compared to RB18 in half-PPR ECR, with 14.4 carries, 3.2 targets and 17.2 half-PPR points in my projection.

No, I do not expect him to continue scoring three touchdowns every 27 touches. That is not the bet. The bet is that Hubbard continues functioning as the bell-cow running back in an improving offense. If that role remains intact, he is an aggressive RB2 start for me in Week 3.

Houston is one of those defenses that looks intimidating when you see the name.

The Texans have already given up quite a few yards through the air against Buffalo and Cincinnati. Obviously, Daniel Jones is not Josh Allen or Joe Burrow, but this is less about expecting Indianapolis to duplicate those offenses and more about identifying where the Colts can attack Houston.

Through two games, Downs has 13 targets, nine catches and 109 receiving yards. The important number for me came last week, when his role expanded to nine targets. He caught seven of them for 72 yards.

Downs is stepping into a primary role inside this passing attack and this is exactly the type of matchup where his skill set can cause problems. Houston has allowed 39 targets and 369 receiving yards to wide receivers through two games. Opposing wide receivers have averaged 43.0 PPR points per game against this defense.

I have Downs projected as WR11 compared to WR38 in consensus rankings, easily the largest gap between my projections and ECR in this article.

I am not telling you that Downs has to be treated like a top-12 wide receiver this week. That is not the point. The point is that WR38 is far too low for the opportunity I expect him to receive.

If you are deciding between Downs and the typical WR3 or flex options, I am getting him into the lineup.

Quinshon Judkins, RB, Browns vs. Panthers

This is the type of matchup Quinshon Judkins needs.

The rushing efficiency has not been there yet. Judkins has 24 carries for only 54 yards through two games. Still, Cleveland continues feeding him the football. He handled 17 touches in Week 2, including five receptions and now has seven catches for 44 yards on the season.

He is the lead back. Now, we need the efficiency to follow.

Carolina gave up a ton of rushing production to D'Andre Swift in Week 1. Atlanta was unable to find the same success last week, but you can't even project them while the inoperable Cooper Rush was at the helm. Had Atlanta been able to present more of a passing threat, there may have been considerably more room for Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. to operate.

Through two games, Carolina has allowed 347 rushing yards and another 59 receiving yards to running backs. Opposing backfields are averaging 36.3 PPR points per game and the Panthers have surrendered 0.114 EPA per rush.

There is also a run-concept piece I really like here.

Inside zone has been Judkins' most-used concept. He has averaged only 2.4 yards per carry on eight attempts, so again, we are not pretending he has been running well. Carolina has allowed 7.1 yards per carry on 13 inside-zone attempts, which RotoBot identifies as the worst rate in the league.

Eight carries and 13 defensive attempts are tiny samples, but the matchup fits what Cleveland already wants Judkins to do.

I have him as my RB21 compared to RB25 in ECR with 14.8 carries, 4.1 targets and 10.6 half-PPR points projected.

Judkins is already getting the work. Against Carolina, this could finally be the week where the production catches up.

Sometimes we do not need to make this more complicated than it needs to be.

The Cowboys have allowed 0.350 EPA per opponent dropback through two games. Tight ends have averaged 16.9 PPR points per game against Dallas and now Baltimore comes to town carrying a 28.0-point implied team total in a game with a 52.5 point total, the highest on the Week 3 slate in the local market snapshot.

That is a good environment for Mark Andrews.

The Cowboys already have enough to worry about dealing with Lamar Jackson as both a passer and runner. Andrews remains one of the more underrated veteran tight ends in football and he is a player Lamar trusts, particularly when the field gets condensed.

Through two games, Andrews has 13 targets, 10 catches and 98 yards. He caught 6-of-7 targets for 49 yards last week and still has not scored a touchdown.

With Zay Flowers likely out, Andrews also becomes even more important in this passing attack alongside Rashod Bateman.

I am not projecting some nuclear tight end performance here. I have Andrews as my TE9 compared to TE12 in ECR with five targets, 9.1 half-PPR points and a little better than a 50 percent projected chance at a touchdown.

This is simply a spot where the player, quarterback and scoring environment all line up. Andrews is a TE1 for me and I like his chances of finally finding the end zone.

Week 3 is where matchup data starts becoming more tempting, but I still do not want the matchup making the decision for me.

Downs is my most aggressive call compared to consensus. Young has earned a spot in your fantasy lineup while this Carolina offense is rolling. Hubbard continues to control a valuable backfield. Judkins finally gets a matchup that could unlock some efficiency and Andrews enters one of the best scoring environments on the slate.

Start with the role. Then use the matchup to decide where to get aggressive.

articles.title: The Pope To Thank For White Sox Playoff Berth? Pope Leo XIV Answers
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV, who's from Chicago and a White Sox fan, was asked what role he played in the team making the playoffs.
articles.body: Divine intervention? With the Chicago White Sox clinching a spot in the MLB playoffs for the first time since 2021 with their Thursday afternoon win against the Kansas City Royals, Pope Leo XIV, who grew up in Chicago and is a fan of the team, was asked whether he played a role in Chicago cracking the American League playoff field this season. "No comment," Leo quipped when asked about what role he played in the White Sox's success, adding that "great things happen in Chicago." Last month, the team had a Pope Leo-White Sox-themed cap giveaway and later sent the hat to the Pope himself, who took a picture with it. While Chicago has punched its ticket to the postseason, its seeding remains up in the air. The White Sox are currently in possession of the No. 3 AL wild-card seed at 82-77, but they trail the Cleveland Guardians by one game for first place in the AL Central. If Chicago wins the AL Central, it will be the No. 3 seed in the AL playoffs and host either Cleveland or the Boston Red Sox in the MLB Wild Card round. Should the Guardians win the AL Central, the White Sox would be the No. 3 AL wild-card seed and travel to Cleveland for the Wild Card round; the Red Sox have the White Sox edged out for the No. 2 AL wild-card seed by way of a tiebreaker (Boston went 6-0 against Chicago this season). Chicago ends the regular season with a three-game series at home against the Colorado Rockies from Sept. 25-27.

articles.title: Red Sox vs. Yankees Wild Card Series Locked In; Here's The Playoff History
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees will meet in the playoffs for the seventh time. Here's the history between the two AL East rivals.
articles.body: It's happening again! The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox will face off in the 2026 MLB Wild Card Series for a second consecutive year, as Boston's Friday afternoon victory over the Chicago Cubs secured its spot as the No. 2 American League wild-card seed; New York secured the No. 1 AL wild-card seed earlier in the week. Game 1 of the three-game set will come on Sept. 29, as the series takes place at Yankee Stadium, like last year when New York defeated Boston in three games. Here's how the two AL East rivals fared against each other this season and their historic postseason history: Yankees Won 2026 Regular-Season Series The Yankees won seven of their 13 games against the Red Sox this season, with New York going 4-2 at home and 3-4 on the road. New York entered Sept. 25 at 92-67, with Boston entering the day at 85-74. .500 Playoff Record The two teams first met in the playoffs in the 1999 AL Championship Series, with the Yankees handling the Red Sox in five games and going on to win the World Series in what was the first season superstar right-hander and then-five-time Cy Young Award winner Roger Clemens, who spent the first 13 seasons of his MLB career with the Red Sox (1984-96), was with the team. Their next postseason meeting came in 2003 in a dramatic showdown that went the distance. A series that included benches clearing in Game 3 and competitive games on the whole ended with a walk-off home run from Yankees third baseman — and now manager — Aaron Boone — to lead off the bottom of the 11th inning of Game 7 in a game where New York trailed 4-0 in the fifth inning. The two teams ran it back the following year (2004), but it had a much different outcome. After going down 3-0 in the series and giving up 19 runs on their home field in Game 3, the Red Sox became the first team in professional sports to win a series after trailing 3-0. Boston then went on to win the World Series for the first time since 1918. The Red Sox and Yankees wouldn't find each other in October again until 2018, with Boston defeating New York 3-1 in the AL Division Series and going on to win the World Series for the fourth time in the 21st century (the Red Sox won the World Series in 2004, 2008, 2013 and 2018). Three years later, Boston made it three consecutive playoff series wins over New York, defeating the Yankees in the 2021 AL Wild Card Game, 6-2. Last year, the Yankees evened the score with the Red Sox at three series wins apiece, winning Games 2 and 3 of the 2025 Wild Card Series to advance to the ALDS.

articles.title: 'It Just Gets Cut Out': Steve Sarkisian On Headset Issues When Trump Attends Games
articles.summary: Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian knows what to expect when President Donald Trump attends Saturday’s game at Tennessee — and it goes well beyond drumming up the atmosphere.
articles.body: Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian knows what to expect when President Donald Trump attends Saturday’s college football game at Tennessee — and it goes well beyond drumming up the atmosphere. Sarkisian said Thursday that coaches can lose headset communication when Trump enters a stadium, leaves the stadium or moves to a different location — something Texas will have to be prepared for when it faces the Volunteers at Neyland Stadium. "The one thing that you have to be aware of when the president goes to any game is that any time he enters the stadium, leaves the stadium or changes locations within the stadium, they cut all communication," Sarkisian said during a Zoom call on Thursday. "So they cut your headsets. They cut the headsets to coaches. They cut headsets for coach-to-player communication. So you have to have a plan for that, if and when it happens, and you get no warning. It just gets cut out." The potential disruption could create challenges for both Texas' offensive and defensive staffs. Defensive coordinator Will Muschamp calls the defense's plays from the sideline, while Sarkisian communicates the offense's plays directly to quarterback Arch Manning. Knowing that could be an issue he has to deal with, Sarkisian reached out to a coaching colleague who has dealt with Trump's presence at the stadium before. He texted Miami head coach Mario Cristobal, seeking guidance of how Cristobal managed Trump attending the 2025 College Football Playoff National Championship Game. "A good friend of mine is Mario Cristobal," Sarkisian said. "Last year, when they were playing Indiana in the national championship, they had that drive at the end of the game; they had no communication because he was leaving early before the game ended. You get no warning; it just cuts out. You have to be prepared for that." Miami ultimately lost the national championship game to Indiana, but Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti pushed back Thursday against claims that a loss of communication led to the final result. Cignetti said Trump's departure did result in a brief communication issue earlier in the fourth quarter. "President Trump left the game around the seven-minute mark in the fourth quarter, there were two or three plays we couldn't hear at all," Cignetti explained on Thursday. "The second play was when they gave the ball to (Malachi) Toney, pitched it to him, for the touchdown with 6:37 to go." "What's floating around on social media is, the communication device went down on Miami's last drive of the game on offense," Cignetti added. "‘Oh really?’ So I had to dispel that." The White House Rapid Response account also disputed the claim that Trump's departure affected Miami's headset communication during the final drive. "No, President Trump's departure from the CFP championship in January did not cause headset or comms issues for the team," the post read. Trump's presence could create an unusual logistical challenge for both teams, and Sarkisian said the key is simply being prepared for the possibility that the headsets could suddenly go silent. "You have to have a plan to adjust if and when he comes in the middle of the first quarter, leaves in the fourth quarter, or decides he’s got to use the restroom, whatever that looks like," Sarkisian said. "You’ve got to be prepared to have no communication for a short amount of time."

articles.title: Yankees Retire Hall of Famer CC Sabathia's No. 52, Gets Monument Park Plaque
articles.summary: Sabathia became the 24th Yankees player or manager to get his number retired and the Hall of Fame left-hander was honored with a plaque in Monument Park.
articles.body: CC Sabathia saw many ceremonies honoring former players during 11 seasons with the New York Yankees and never envisioned he would be an honoree. Sabathia became the 24th player or manager to get his number retired and the Hall of Fame left-hander was honored with a plaque in Monument Park during a ceremony before a doubleheader opener against Baltimore on Friday. Sabathia joined Derek Jeter, Mariano Rivera, Andy Pettitte and Jorge Posada as the fifth member of 2009 World Series champion Yankees with a retired number and plaque. "I never envisioned myself going into Monument Park and I think that was the reason why I was so scared to come here is because you don’t ever think you’re going to win the Yankee fans over or the city over," Sabathia said. "So to be able to be sitting here now, playing here 11 years is an incredible feeling and that’s why I’ve said the last couple of weeks, this feels bigger to me than the Hall of Fame because I know what was at stake when I came here." Now 46, Sabathia signed a $161 million, seven-year contract before the 2009 season after being convinced by general manager Brian Cashman following an initial meeting in December 2008. The contract was the largest at the time for a free-agent pitcher. Sabathia went 19-8 with a 3.37 ERA in 34 starts for the Yankees in his first season. He earned the AL Championship Series MVP Award, going 2-0 with a 1.13 ERA in a six-game win over the Los Angeles Angels and started Games 1 and 4 as the Yankees beat Philadelphia for their 27th title. Sabathia went 251-161 with a 3.74 ERA and 3,093 strikeouts, third among left-handers behind Randy Johnson and Steve Carlton, during 19 seasons with Cleveland (2001-08), Milwaukee (2008) and the Yankees (2009-19). During 11 seasons in New York, Sabathia was 134-88 with a 3.81 ERA and 1,700 strikeouts. He ranks fourth in franchise history in strikeouts, seventh in starts, 10th in wins and 11th in innings. Sabathia was a first-ballot Hall of Famer in 2025, receiving 86.8% of the vote. He was inducted with Billy Wagner and Ichiro Suzuki, a former Yankee teammate from 2012-14. "That ceremony was incredible, surreal," Sabathia said. "I was saying out there I have so many famous teammates whether it’s Mo, Derek, Andy. So I’ve been at the ceremony a bunch of times but to have that ceremony be for me is special and to have my family out there was cool." The Yankees' ceremony began with video messages from Jeter, Paul O’Neill, Jorge Posada and Bernie Williams, and Sabathia unveiled the plaque with his wife Amber, two of his children, two friends and his mother, Margie. After video highlights, Sabathia waved to fans from a golf cart along the warning track. He was presented with a blue blazer, a framed version of his plaque and retired number along with a ring commemorating his career from general manager Brian Cashman — who was booed by fans. After the ceremony, Sabathia threw out the ceremonial first pitch to his son Carsten, a Milwaukee minor league first baseman. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: ‘Kabaddi Kabaddi’ in Japan as India’s gold-hungry teams march on at Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: “Kabaddi Kabaddi,” the superhit Tamil number from superstar-turned-chief minister Vijay’s film ‘Ghilli’ played on a loop in the otherwise quiet Japanese
articles.body: “Kabaddi Kabaddi,” the superhit Tamil number from superstar-turned-chief minister Vijay’s film ‘Ghilli’ played on a loop in the otherwise quiet Japanese air. Vanakams and namastes rent from the stands, while the unmistakable aroma of chhole and kebabs hung in the air.No, this isn’t India. But this is kabaddi, at the Tokai Citizen Gymnasium, venue for the competition where both Indian men’s and women’s teams are favourites at the Asian Games.A sizable Indian diaspora, Indian officials and technical staff, along with members of the Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India and the Indian Olympic Association, added to the Indian flavour. The Indian teams completed the picture, taking another step towards defending their crowns with comfortable semifinals wins on Friday. The men beat Thailand 37-18, 29-10, while the women overcame Nepal 31-17, 17-7.For the teams, anything short of gold simply isn’t enough. Over the years, between them, they have contributed 11 Asian Games gold medals to India’s tally, eight of them coming from the men. “India has set the gold standard, so why settle for something less?” quipped Indian women’s vice captain Sonali Shingate.The 30-year-old, however, insists that ambition does not translate into pressure. “We have more responsibility than pressure. When you are the best team in the world, it’s not just about a podium finish. We don’t want to settle for anything but gold. There is no other target,” said the raider. Sonali believes the intensity of domestic kabaddi prepares Indian players well for international competition.“We don’t feel that much pressure in international tournaments because we experience more of it in national competitions, given how keenly they are fought,” she said, recalling India’s 37-23 win over Iran as their toughest league outing.She also credits the franchise league in the country for making the sport more competitive globally, with foreign players learning alongside and against Indian stars.For Sonali, that growing competition is no threat to India’s dominance. articles.title: Asian Games: Anahat Singh saves two match points to stun world No. 6 Satomi Watanabe, now one win away from historic gold and LA Olympics
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian squash sensation Anahat Singh produced the biggest victory of her career, fighting back from two games down to defeat Japan’s world No.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian squash sensation Anahat Singh produced the biggest victory of her career, fighting back from two games down to defeat Japan’s world No. 6 Satomi Watanabe and storm into the women’s singles final at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday. The 18-year-old is now just one win away from a historic gold medal and a place at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where squash will make its debut.The world No. 17 Indian, playing in front of a home crowd supporting Watanabe, showed extraordinary resilience to prevail 9-11, 11-13, 12-10, 11-6, 11-3 in a gripping five-game semifinal at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena. Anahat’s victory also avenged her earlier five-game defeat to the Japanese star this year.The stakes could hardly be higher. The Asian Games singles competitions serve as the Asian continental qualification event for the LA Olympics, giving Anahat an opportunity to secure a place at squash’s first appearance on the Olympic programme.Anahat saves two match points to turn the contest aroundAnahat’s route to the final was anything but straightforward. Watanabe, the home favourite, used her variations, changes of pace and sharp angles to take the opening two games, leaving the Indian with a daunting challenge.The teenager, however, refused to surrender. Trailing 8-10 in the third game, she saved two match points before fighting back to win 12-10 and keep her hopes alive.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleThe contest also featured an unfortunate collision between the two players. As Anahat attempted to retrieve a ball, her head collided with Watanabe’s shoulder, prompting a brief stoppage for medical attention. After receiving treatment, the Indian returned to the court and continued her fightback.With the momentum swinging her way, Anahat dominated the fourth game, winning it 11-6 to level the match at 2-2. In the deciding game, she was in complete control, attacking confidently and denying Watanabe an opportunity to recover. Anahat raced to an 11-3 win to complete a remarkable comeback and book her place in the final.The victory marks a significant milestone in the young Indian’s career, as she now has an opportunity to win the Asian Games title and take a major step towards the Olympic stage.Historic gold and Olympic qualification within reachWith squash set to make its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028, the Asian Games singles events carry added significance. The continental competition provides a qualification pathway for Asian players, placing Anahat on the brink of a potentially historic achievement.The Indian teenager’s final appearance also offers her an opportunity to build on the progress she has made on the international circuit. Having overcome one of the tournament’s leading contenders in her own backyard, she will now look to carry that momentum into the gold-medal match.Earlier in the day, India’s Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar had to settle for bronze in the mixed doubles after losing a closely fought semifinal against Hong Kong’s Tang Ming Hong and Lee Ka Yi.The Indian pair went down 10-11, 11-2, 10-11 in an intense three-game contest. After narrowly losing the opening game, Joshna and Velavan responded emphatically to take the second, but Hong Kong held their nerve in the deciding game to reach the final.Anahat’s victory, however, ensured that India’s hopes of a squash gold remained alive, with the teenager now one match away from adding a landmark title to her growing list of achievements.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pressure to boycott Israel game grows as Ireland preparations stall
articles.summary: Ireland are due to play Israel in the Nations League in Hungary on Sunday, but boycott pressure mounts on and off-field.
articles.body:
The Ireland team’s news conference and training session the day before its first Nations League game against Israel have been delayed as pressure to boycott the matches grows.

Journalists in Debrecen, Hungary – where Israel’s “home” game is to be played Sunday – were left waiting Saturday after being told the news conference was being pushed back until after training. That was 15 minutes before it was supposed to begin.

Training was also significantly delayed, however, with Irish broadcaster RTE reporting the players were still in their hotel more than two hours after the training session was supposed to begin.

RTE reported that some players had decided they did not want to play the games.

“And if they stay to their stated ambition that they have to be all in it together, if one or more want to be out, maybe they will all be out,” reporter Tony O’Donoghue told RTE Radio 1.

The team has been coming under increasing pressure in Ireland, where affinity with Palestinians is strong, to boycott the two games – the first on Sunday and the second, Ireland’s “home” game, in Backa Topola, Serbia, on October 4.

Ireland midfielder Jason Knight said after Thursday’s 1-0 loss in Kosovo that the players were in a difficult situation and that he didn’t think the matches should be going ahead.

Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson previously said “we’re not playing with genocide, we’re playing against genocide. We’re playing against Israel, we’re not playing with Israel” – drawing a furious reaction from the Israeli football federation, which accused the Icelandic coach of “stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy”.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had resisted calls to boycott the matches, arguing the team could be hit by punishing sanctions by UEFA. Ireland is cohosting the 2028 European Championship with England, Wales and Scotland.

More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter urging the FAI to reconsider its decision to go ahead with the fixtures.

There were protesters outside the team hotel in Dublin last week calling on the players to boycott the games. The SIPTU trade union displayed a huge poster in central Dublin beside the River Liffey asking the players to “Go with your conscience!” and “Don’t play with genocide” beside an image of a blood-splattered ball.

Former Ireland coach Brian Kerr said the FAI had “lost the respect of the Irish people” for going ahead with the games.

“The Irish people and the soccer-going public don’t want the games to be played,” Kerr said. “I think they’ve made their opinions clear over the last year. The FAI back in November actually went to UEFA and requested that Israel be put out of the tournament on principle. And yet they went against that principle.”

articles.title: Ordenan cambiar el nombre de un caballo de carreras por referirse a Hitler
articles.standfirst: El animal se llamaba 'Austrian Painter', denominación que se usa para referirse veladamente al dictador alemán
articles.summary: El animal se llamaba 'Austrian Painter', denominación que se usa para referirse veladamente al dictador alemán
articles.body: El Jockey Club de Estados Unidos ordenó el cambio de nombre de un caballo de carreras al considerar que era una clara referencia a Adolf Hitler. Todo arrancó cuando 'Austrian Painter', ejemplar de 2 años, ganó su carrera de debut en el hipódromo Horseshoe de Indianápolis a principios de esta semana. El Jockey Club recibió una queja e inició una investigación, tal y como anunció 'Horse Racing Nation'. En Internet se suele usar el término 'Austrian Painter' para referirse a Hitler (fue pintor profesional en Viena antes de la Primera Guerra Mundial) sin mencionarlo por su nombre y así evitar los filtros de moderación de contenido. Scott Herbertson, propietario y criador del potro de dos años, comentó en redes sociales que el nombre se debía al artista austriaco Gustav Klimt y que no lo iba a cambiar. Además, 'Austrian Painter' tiene una hermana de un año llamada 'New Order', nombre de una banda de rock británica pero que también alude al término que la Alemania nazi utilizó para su plan de reorganización de la Europa ocupada. El Jockey Club indicó también que la yegua debía cambiar su nombre. "New Order es mi banda favorita, ¿sabes?", se defendió Herbertson. Además, según apunta 'Defector', Herbertson había presentado otros nombres al Jockey Club en su momento para 'Austrian Painter' con referencias hitlerianas: 'My Struggle', traducción al inglés del manifiesto de Hitler, 'Mein Kampf', que escribió en prisión; y 'Braunau Star', que podría ser una alusión a Braunau am Inn, lugar de nacimiento de Hitler, aunque Herbertson afirmó que se refería a la ciudad donde vino al mundo el abuelo de su esposa El Jockey Club argumenta su decisión de acuerdo su reglamento. "El nombre no cumple con los requisitos de la Regla 6.F.9.d, que prohíbe los nombres que ‘pueden resultar ofensivos o amenazantes por motivos que incluyen, entre otros, color, credo, discapacidad, etnia, género, origen nacional, raza, religión, política u orientación sexual", indicó en un comunicado al tiempo que resaltaba que "nos tomamos estos asuntos muy en serio y agradecemos que se nos hayan comunicado". El nuevo nombre del caballo será 'Merrylegs'. Dado que 'Austrian Painter' ya ha comenzado su carrera, la Regla 6(D) exige que se utilicen ambos nombres, el prohibido y el nuevo, hasta que complete tres carreras.

articles.title: Egypt to rest Salah in South Sudan AFCON qualifier over pitch concerns
articles.summary: Egyptian FA has decided to rest Salah to protect him from playing on artificial turf, which is likelier to cause injury.
articles.body:
Mohamed Salah will not travel with ⁠Egypt’s ⁠squad to South Sudan for their second Africa Cup of Nations qualifier because the ⁠match will be played on artificial turf, the Egyptian Football Association said ⁠on Saturday.

Record seven-time AFCON champions Egypt were held to a goalless draw by Angola at Cairo International Stadium on Friday in their opening qualifier.

Two-time African Footballer of the Year, Salah, who ‌joined Turkiye’s Trabzonspor from Liverpool last month, started against Angola but did not complete the match after coach Hossam Hassan substituted him midway through the second half.

“The Egypt national team’s technical staff, led by Hossam Hassan, has ⁠decided to rest Mohamed Salah ⁠for the match against South Sudan scheduled for September 29 because of the playing surface,” the EFA said on social ⁠media .

“It was agreed between the national team’s technical staff and ⁠Mohamed Salah before the Angola ⁠match that he would not play against South Sudan, and the technical staff preferred this approach in order to ‌protect the player,” the EFA added.

Salah has scored 68 goals for Egypt and is just one short of matching coach and ex-player Hassan’s all-time record of 69 for The Pharaohs.

Tuesday’s match between South Sudan and Egypt will be played ‌at ‌Juba Stadium, which has an artificial turf pitch. Such surfaces pose a higher risk of injuries than those with natural grass.

Egypt are in Group B of the AFCON 2027 qualifiers, alongside Angola, South Sudan and Malawi. The 2027 AFCON will be co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania, featuring 24 teams.

Though Egypt are the most successful African side, they haven’t won the championship since 2010.

articles.title: Russell edges out Verstappen to win in Baku, Antonelli settles for fifth
articles.summary: George Russell wins Azerbaijan Grand Prix for eighth career F1 victory and first since the Austrian GP in June.
articles.body:
George Russell held off Red Bull’s four-time world champion Max Verstappen to complete a lights-to-flag win in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix for Mercedes, with teammate Kimi Antonelli limiting the damage to his championship lead by finishing fifth.

Russell took the flag 0.196 seconds ahead of the flying Dutchman, who started eighth but crossed the line nearly side-by-side with his Mercedes rival after two safety car phases turned a cruise into a fight for survival for the Briton.

Frenchman Isack Hadjar, who was handed a contract extension by Red Bull earlier this week and had missed the last three races with a wrist injury, completed the podium on his racing return.

The win around the Baku street track was the eighth of Russell’s career, the third of the season and his first since the Austrian Grand Prix at the end of June.

It allowed him to close the gap in the overall standings to Italian championship leader Antonelli by 15 points to 66 after 15 rounds.

“It’s amazing to be back on the top step of the podium,” said Russell.

“Every race since the (summer) break I’ve gone from strength to strength and I feel more like myself again.”

Antonelli had started 16th after a rare error saw him crash out of Friday’s qualifying.

His drive on Saturday was less like his Monza charge — where he went from 19th to first — and more of a slow-burn recovery.

Charles Leclerc took fourth for Ferrari ahead of the 20-year-old Italian. His seven-time world champion teammate Lewis Hamilton was sixth.

Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad finished seventh. Esteban Ocon took eighth ahead of teammate Oliver Bearman in a double points finish for Haas.

Carlos Sainz rounded out the top 10 for Williams.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 7: India win seven medals as kabaddi teams deliver gold double in action-packed Saturday
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed one of its most productive days at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, winning seven medals with the kabaddi teams providing the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed one of its most productive days at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, winning seven medals with the kabaddi teams providing the biggest highlights by successfully defending their respective gold medals.The men defeated Iran 40-34 in a hard-fought final, while the women also overcame Iran 37-34 to complete a memorable kabaddi gold double for India. The men's triumph was their ninth Asian Games gold in the sport, while the women's victory brought their tally to four.India's seven-medal haul also included a historic silver for marathon runner Sawan Barwal, silver medals for Tajinderpal Singh Toor and the women's 50m rifle 3 positions team, and bronze medals for Prachi Choudhary in the women's 400m and Joshna Chinappa-Velavan Senthilkumar in squash.The day's results took India's overall medal tally to 30 — four gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleBarwal delivers historic marathon silverThe day began with one of India's biggest surprises when Sawan Barwal produced a stunning run to win silver in the men's marathon and break his own national record.The 28-year-old Armyman from Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, completed the 42.195km race in 2 hours, 11 minutes and 37 seconds to finish behind Japan's Ichitaka Yamashita, who won gold in 2:10:49. China's Peiyou Feng took bronze in 2:12:13.Barwal's silver was India's first Asian Games marathon medal since Hosur Kukkappa Seetharan's bronze in the 1982 edition in New Delhi. He also became only the fourth Indian marathon runner to win an Asian Games medal.Chhota Singh had won gold and Surat Singh Mathur bronze at the inaugural Asian Games in 1951, while Seetharan's bronze came three decades later.ALSO READ: How two kabaddi golds helped India break back into top 10Kabaddi teams maintain their grip on goldIndia's kabaddi campaign once again ended with both teams on top of the podium, although neither final was straightforward.The women held their nerve to beat Iran 37-34, while the men recovered from a closely fought first half to defeat the same opponents 40-34.The men's gold was India's ninth in the sport at the Asian Games, underlining their long-standing dominance, while the women's team retained the title they had won at Hangzhou.The two victories accounted for India's only gold medals of the day and provided a major boost to the country's medal count.Shooting and athletics add three more medalsAt the shooting range, Tilottama Sen, Vidarsa Vinod and Ashi Chouksey won silver in the women's 50m rifle 3 positions team event.The Indian trio aggregated 1763 points to finish behind China, who set a Games Record of 1773 for gold. Kazakhstan took bronze with 1754.Tilottama and Vidarsa also reached the individual final but narrowly missed the podium, finishing fourth and fifth respectively.In athletics, Prachi Choudhary added a bronze in the women's 400m, clocking 53.21 seconds. Bahrain's Salwa Naser won gold in a Games Record 49.20 seconds, while Iran's Zahra Zarei Manoujan took silver in 52.38 seconds.There was disappointment too, as two-time defending champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor had to settle for silver in the men's shot put. His 20.64m throw was well below his personal best of 21.77m.Iran's Mohammadreza Tayebise won gold with a Games Record 20.81m, breaking Toor's previous Games mark of 20.75m.Anahat, Abhay keep squash gold hopes aliveIndia's squash campaign received a major boost as Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh stormed into their respective singles finals.The 18-year-old Anahat produced one of the biggest wins of her career, coming from 0-2 down to stun world No. 6 Satomi Watanabe of Japan 9-11, 11-13, 12-10, 11-6, 11-3.Abhay followed by sweeping Pakistan's Muhammad Irfan 11-3, 12-10, 11-6 to reach the men's final.A gold for either player would also bring the prospect of qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where squash will make its debut.Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar had earlier secured India's bronze in mixed doubles after losing 1-2 to Hong Kong's Tang Ming Hong and Lee Ka Yi.Hockey, archery provide further positivesThe men's hockey team reached the semifinals after beating Japan 2-0 in its penultimate pool match.India also made a strong start to its archery campaign. Dhiraj Bommadevara topped the men's recurve individual qualification with 698 points, setting a new Asian Games qualification record. articles.title: Nathan MacKinnon’s $100.8 million Colorado Avalanche contract made NHL history: The numbers behind his extraordinary career earnings and record-setting deal
articles.summary: Explore the groundbreaking $100.8 million contract extension of Nathan MacKinnon with the Colorado Avalanche, analyzing its impact on the NHL salary landscape, his extraordinary career earnings, and on-ice performance milestones.
articles.body: Nathan MacKinnon’s financial ascent has mirrored his rise as one of the more productive centers in the NHL. Selected first overall in the 2013 NHL Draft by the Colorado Avalanche, his career has included a Stanley Cup, major individual awards and multiple seasons in the top 10 in scoring in the league.His financial story hit the spotlight in September of 2022 when the Colorado Avalanche announced an eight-year, $100.8 million contract extension. The deal, announced Tuesday, has an average annual value of $12.6 million, making MacKinnon the NHL’s highest-paid player by annual value at the time of signing.Nathan MacKinnon’s massive Colorado Avalanche contract reshaped NHL financesColorado Avalanche signs Nathan MacKinnon to eight-year extension Sept. 20, 2022. The deal runs through the 2030-31 season and is worth $100.8 million over seven years (2023-24 to 2030-31). Its annual average value of $12.6 million was a major increase from MacKinnon’s previous seven-year, $44.1 million extension.MacKinnon’s last contract was an average of $6.3 million annually. His annual average value doubled with the new deal, to $12.6 million, which is where he was as a franchise centrepiece and one of the NHL’s elite offensive players.Contract detailNathan MacKinnonTeamColorado AvalancheContract term8 yearsTotal value$100.8 millionStart2023-24End2030-31Average annual value$12.6 millionSigning bonuses$85.34 millionPrevious contract7 years, $44.1 millionPrevious AAV$6.3 millionThe timing was also a point of importance with the contract. The Avalanche had just won the 2022 Stanley Cup, and MacKinnon was already one of Colorado’s most important players when the deal was done. The deal essentially tied the organization’s long-term plans to a player who had become a centrepiece of its championship core.At the time of the deal, MacKinnon’s 12.6 million AAV put him above Connor McDavid’s then-12.5 million cap hit. That instantly made the contract an NHL financial benchmark, though subsequent contracts around the league have altered the salary landscape.Nathan MacKinnon’s contract structure and signing bonuses explainedOne of the more interesting elements of the MacKinnon deal is the amounts set aside for signing bonuses. Spotrac says signing bonuses over the course of the eight years come out to $85.34 million, leaving a much smaller chunk as traditional base salary.In particular, the structure loads up large cash payments in the opening seasons. MacKinnon's 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons will include a base salary of $775,000 and signing bonus money of $15.725 million. The deal also featured a $15.25 million signing bonus and a $800,000 salary for the 2025-26 season, which generated $16.05 million in scheduled cash for that season.Contract seasonBase salarySigning bonusScheduled cash2023-24$775,000$15.725 million$16.5 million2024-25$775,000$15.725 million$16.5 million2025-26$800,000$15.25 million$16.05 million2026-27$9.15 million$3 million$12.15 million2027-28$990,000$8.91 million$9.9 million2028-29$990,000$8.91 million$9.9 million2029-30$990,000$8.91 million$9.9 million2030-31$990,000$8.91 million$9.9 millionThat's a big difference between cash salary and salary-cap accounting. MacKinnon has a $12.6 million cap hit, but his scheduled cash compensation deviates significantly from that figure in several seasons. The way the NHL collective bargaining process deals with signing bonuses means contracts can have a different distribution of actual payments than their annual cap charge.PuckPedia does have some minor tweaks to some of the later-year salary figures, including a $1 million base salary in the final seasons and an adjusted average annual value of approximately $12.604 million those years. Still, the headline value of the deal is $100.8 million over eight seasons.The arrangement also demonstrates why an NHL contract cannot be simply understood by dividing total value by the number of seasons. That $12.6 million AAV is based on cap-related figures, but the actual cash flow in individual years varies based on the structure of the signing bonus.Nathan MacKinnon’s NHL earnings and career impact through 2026MacKinnon was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2013 NHL Draft and signed a three-year entry-level deal with Colorado before signing his current seven-year, $44.1 million contract extension that runs from 2016-17 to 2022-23. Spotrac projects his total cash earnings to be about $101.84 million through the 2025 calendar year.This number shows the speed at which the earnings accelerated after the start of the $100.8 million extension. Spotrac’s contract breakdown shows MacKinnon received $16.5 million in cash in each of the first two years of the extension and $16.05 million in the third. Payments scheduled then decline as the contract approaches its final seasons.The cash value of MacKinnon’s NHL contracts listed is roughly $153.6 million through the end of the current extension if the scheduled contract payments are made in full. The figure is a contract-based projection, not a statement of money earned, nor is it an estimate of taxes, agent fees or personal expenses.Earnings milestoneAmountFirst NHL contract$11.325 million2016 extension$44.1 million2023 extension$100.8 millionCareer cash through 2025$101.84 millionScheduled total through 2030-31$153.59 millionMacKinnon’s on-ice production has continued to put his contract into perspective too. In 2023-24, he scored a career-best 140 points with 51 goals and 89 assists, winning the Hart Memorial Trophy and Ted Lindsay Award. The Colorado Avalanche also point out that he has since become the franchise’s all-time points leader.So the financial story is more than just the headline $100.8 million. MacKinnon’s contract was a mix of an NHL-record annual value at the time of signing and a heavily bonus-driven payment structure, and his production has continued to keep him among the league’s leading offensive players. The Republic of Ireland will play their Nations League fixture against Israel on Sunday after a vote ⁠within the squad on whether to fulfil the fixture, Football Association of Ireland (FAI) CEO David Courell said on Saturday.

Ireland had postponed their pre-match news conference ahead of the game in Hungary, and their training ⁠session was also delayed.

This was to allow further talks to continue between Irish players, coaching staff and executives, after one player announced their intention to withdraw from the squad.

“This morning, a player expressed their discomfort with fulfilling this fixture to the head coach and indicated their intent to withdraw from the ‌squad,” Courell told reporters.

“Ultimately, within the last maybe 90 minutes, we carried out a vote amongst the squad to establish their sentiment on fulfilling the fixtures, and it was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue.

“So based on that, the association took the decision on behalf of Irish football that this fixture would continue, as we have always intended to fulfil the fixtures.”

Ireland were due to hold the news conference on Saturday but shortly before ⁠the scheduled start at 10:15am local time (08:15 GMT), reporters were informed ⁠that this would now take place following the team’s training session at the stadium in Debrecen.

That was due to commence at 11am local time, but more than three hours later, the Ireland team were still inside their hotel.

Ahead of Ireland’s opening ⁠Group B3 game away to Kosovo, which they lost 1-0, captain Dara O’Shea told reporters that the players would meet on Friday to discuss a ⁠plan of action for the game against Israel.

FAI members voted in ⁠November for its board to request that UEFA suspend Israel from European competitions, but a motion in favour of proceeding with the fixtures was passed at an FAI EGM in July.

All of Israel’s home games are scheduled to take place in Debrecen, ‌and Ireland moved their home fixture, set for October 4, to Serbia. That game will be played behind closed doors.

Tensions increased further when Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson used the word “genocide” in a media conference ‌last ‌weekend. The Israeli FA responded by calling his remarks stupid, ignorant and hypocritical.

Israel’s war on Gaza has been described as genocide by United Nations experts and rights organisations, an allegation Israel strongly rejects.

articles.title: Manuel Ochoa, bronce en la crono del kayak cros individual en el Europeo
articles.standfirst: Es la primera medalla del gallego en un campeonato internacional de primer nivel
articles.summary: Es la primera medalla del gallego en un campeonato internacional de primer nivel
articles.body: Manuel Ochoa logró la medalla de bronce en la contrarreloj individual masculina de kayak cros en los Europeos de piragüismo eslalon, que se disputan en Ivrea (Italia), con un tiempo de 43.90 segundos. El oro fue para el italiano Giovanni De Gennaro, con un tiempo de 43.29 segundos. El podio lo completó el francés Mathurin Madoré (43.41), plata. Es la primera medalla para España en estos Europeos, después de que no consiguiera metales ni en canoa ni en kayak. El equipo español ha sumado al menos una presea en todos los Europeos de piragüismo eslalon desde la edición de 2021. También es la primera medalla en un campeonato internacional de primer nivel (Europeos o Mundiales) para Ochoa, que había firmado una buena temporada en Copa del Mundo este 2026, con un oro en la contrarreloj individual en Augsburgo y sendas platas en esta modalidad en Vaires-sur-Marne y La Seu d'Urgell. Ochoa comenzó su bajada cuando faltaban menos de una decena de competidores. Empezó en un estado de forma similar al de su curso de Copa del Mundo y fue el más rápido de los palistas hasta el momento en el segundo intervalo. Terminó con un tiempo de 43.90 segundos que lo colocaba provisionalmente en la segunda posición. Estaba sólo por detrás del italiano Giovanni De Gennaro (43.29), vigente campeón olímpico de K1 individual. El gallego, de 27 años, tenía que esperar a los resultados de sus rivales. Según avanzaban el resto de las bajadas, sus opciones de medalla fueron en aumento, al ver que nadie mejoraba su registro. Solo Mathurin Madoré (43.41) fue capaz de colarse en el podio por delante del español, que se hizo con el bronce. En la tarde de este sábado se disputan las eliminatorias de kayak cros, última prueba del campeonato continental. Con los resultados de la contrarreloj, Pau Echaniz (46.77) y David Llorente (45.79) también se clasificaron para las series en categoría masculina, y Miren Lazkano (51.50), Leire Goñi (51.72) y Laia Sorribes (51.96) lo hicieron en la femenina.

articles.title: 'Khali pet gold jita hai': Why India's kabaddi team did not eat before Asian Games final
articles.summary: India’s men’s kabaddi team had one thing on their mind before the Asian Games final - winning gold.
articles.body: India’s men’s kabaddi team had one thing on their mind before the Asian Games final - winning gold.So much so that the players did not eat properly before their title clash against Iran.“Khali pet gold jita hai,” captain Pawan Sehrawat said after India defeated Iran 40-34 to retain their Asian Games men’s kabaddi title on Saturday.‘Those 40 minutes were important’India had prepared well for the final, but Pawan knew the result would only be decided on the mat.“I was very excited about the match. I was very excited about what was going to happen in the match in the evening. Even if we know that we are playing well, we have practised well. But until the result comes, it stays in the mind. Those 40 minutes were important,” Pawan told IANS.India went into half-time trailing 17-18 but produced a strong second-half performance to turn the match around.Arjun Deshwal and Devank Dalal led the attack, while Sumit and Jaideep played important roles in defence.India turn the final aroundWith 10 minutes left, India moved five points ahead after Arjun got past Iran captain Fazel Atrachali and helped India inflict an All-Out.Sumit then made an important tackle on Amirmohammad Zafar Danesh, while Rahul Sethpal also made a key defensive contribution late in the match.The win completed India's unbeaten campaign and gave them their ninth Asian Games gold medal in men's kabaddi.For Pawan, however, the wait for the result made the final even more emotional.“Everyone is emotional, so I get emotional at such moments. And it was that once the 40 minutes are over, we will eat and drink well. Not just one, but after that gold has come,” he said.Keeping an eye on India’s medal tallyPawan also revealed that the players were following India's position on the medal table during the Games.“We were seeing on the way that if our two golds are added, then where will we go? Till that time, as far as I could see, we were in sixth. And since then, we have not used the mobile properly. I don't know which number we will have in our medal tally,” he said.Gold medal dedicated to coachPawan credited his coach Randhir Sehrawat for playing a major role in his success and dedicated the gold medal to him.“I would like to dedicate it to my coach Randhir Sehrawat. Because it is because of him that this medal has come to me,” he said.He also urged the government to consider Randhir for the Dronacharya Award, pointing out that several Arjuna Award winners had trained under him.‘Japan has created history for me’Pawan, who was one of India’s flag-bearers at the opening ceremony alongside Manu Bhaker, also spoke about his experience in Japan.“Japan is very beautiful. For me, Japan has created history. I was a flag bearer. I was with such a good athlete, Manu Bhaker. articles.title: Lula y Brasil declaran la guerra a las apuestas por internet
articles.standfirst: El candidato opositor Bolsonaro apoya en parte la medida
articles.summary: El candidato opositor Bolsonaro apoya en parte la medida
articles.body: Hasta ahora, las prohibiciones y/o restricciones a las apuestas deportivas por internet -que se han convertido en uno de los 'poderes fácticos' del deporte moderno por el ingente volumen económico que movilizan– era cosa de países como Arabia Saudí, Emiratos Árabes, Qatar o Irán, por su tradición islámica y algunos estados de India o China y Corea del Norte. A estos estados se une ahora otro de gran peso tanto en volumen económico como en la actividad deportiva: Brasil. No sólo el gobierno del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ha anunciado nueve días antes de las elecciones presidenciales y legislativas la prohibición en el país de las apuestas deportivas y los casinos en línea, sino que el candidato opositor, el ultraderechista Flavio Bolsonaro, apoya en parte la iniciativa. El mandatario ha anunciado la prohibición definitiva de todas las apuestas digitales, a partir del 6 de octubre, y la publicidad de sus empresas, por medio de un decreto que entrará en vigor en cuanto se publique en el Diario Oficial, aunque el Parlamento tendrá que convalidarlo en un plazo máximo de 120 días. Además se tipificará esta actividad como delito contemplado en el código penal. El motivo fundamental es que el presidente Lula da Silva y su gobierno atribuyen a las apuestas un importante papel en el crecimiento del endeudamiento de las familias, acusándoles de "estar destruyendo millones de hogares" al transformar "el vicio en beneficio económico". Además, se ampliará el actual programa de renegociación de deudas. No entra en este debate, por tanto, las amenazas e insultos a muchos deportistas por parte de apostadores incompetentes al ver fallar sus pronósticos. Las casas de apuestas en línea se legalizaron en Brasil en 2018 pero tuvieron su primera regulación en 2023, ya con Lula en el poder. Según informa Efe, en 2025 cerca de 25 millones de brasileños apostaron 220.600 millones de reales (42.500 millones de dólares / 37.150 millones de euros al cambio de hoy) en apuestas deportivas y casinos en línea. Las empresas afectadas señalan que esta decisión irá en contra de la protección a los jugadores. En un manifiesto conjunto han señalado que la gran mayoría de brasileños apuestan de modo responsable y que ya trabajan en la prevención del endeudamiento de la familias: "el mercado legal impide que 3 millones de beneficiarios de programas sociales apuesten y ya atendió 1,2 millones de pedidos de autoexclusión", además de señalar que los apostadores recurrirán ahora a portales ilegales, donde no existe ningún tipo de protección. Una traslación que sucede, por otra parte, en muchos de los otros países que han prohibido la actividad. La medida ha sido también criticada por clubes de fútbol, muchos de ellos patrocinados por portales de apuestas. De hecho, el campeonato Brasileirao lo está por el portal Betano. Lula ha comparado a las apuestas con la drogadicción: "es algo espeluznante; me recordó al comienzo del 'crack' en este país. Las apuestas en línea son lo mismo, pero a un nivel muy superior porque son digitales y están al alcance de la mano". El senador y candidato opositor Flávio Bolsonaro, hijo del anterior presidente ultraderechista Jair Bolsonaro, condenado por los tribunales por planear un golpe de estado, acusó a presidente de "estafa electoral", dado que su gobierno cobró impuestos a las empresas de apuestas tras su legalización. Sin embargo, ha anunciado que si es elegido presidente abolirá los casinos virtuales, aunque no aclaró si permitirá las apuestas deportivas.

articles.title: Manchester City confident they can prove ‘innocence’ over charges: Chairman
articles.summary: Man City to appeal 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules, chairman says club is confident of success.
articles.body:
Manchester ‌‌‌‌City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said the club is confident of proving their innocence, the ⁠⁠⁠⁠day after media reported ⁠⁠⁠that ⁠City had been found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules in a long-running case.

In an open letter to supporters on Saturday, Al Mubarak ⁠⁠⁠⁠said the process was far from over and City’s confidence in proving the club’s innocence “is just as strong as when this began”.

“Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening ⁠⁠⁠⁠answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I,” Al Mubarak said.

“Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.”

City, who ‌‌‌‌have always denied any wrongdoing, are expected to appeal the decision of the independent panel in a case that has hung over English football for years.

A guilty verdict would rank among the most significant rulings in the sport’s history, raising far-reaching questions about financial regulation, competitive integrity and the league’s ability to enforce its rules against one of its most successful clubs.

Al Mubarak said he was limited in what he could say about the case because of the strict confidentiality ⁠⁠⁠⁠of the legal process.

“Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make ⁠⁠⁠⁠sure it complies,” he said.

“I ask you to please carefully read the statement … which we gave on Friday and the statement we issued in February 2023 …” which he included in the open letter. “Every word matters and holds true.”

The February 2023 ⁠⁠⁠⁠statement said the club was surprised by the alleged breaches, “particularly given the extensive engagement and vast amount of detailed materials that the EPL (English Premier League) ⁠⁠⁠⁠has been provided with.

“The club welcomes the review of this ⁠⁠⁠⁠matter by an independent commission, to impartially consider the comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of its position.”

City reiterated that statement on Friday.

The Premier League has declined to comment.

“It’s a confidential process, we’re not commenting at all,” a spokesperson ‌‌‌‌said.

Al Mubarak asked for patience from supporters.

“While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed,” he said.

“We have faced challenges ‌‌‌‌together ‌‌‌‌before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.”

articles.body:
The Montreal Canadiens are set to face the Ottawa Senators in split games that will be played simultaneously on Saturday, with one match up taking place at the Bell Centre, and the other at the Canadian Tire Centre. Both games are scheduled to begin at 7 pm ET.

It will be the final preseason opportunity for several NHL hopefuls, including defenceman David Reinbacher , and forward Florian Xhekaj, the two players who have the best odds of making the team out of camp.

Reinbacher is aiming to earn a job on the blue line, a situation that has been helped along by Kaiden Guhle 's absence. Guhle is expected to miss another four weeks of action as he recovers from his latest surgery. Reinbacher is set to play in Ottawa, paired with yet another defenceman with NHL aspirations, the smooth-skating Adam Engstrom .

The pairing will play second fiddle to Arber Xhekaj and Jayden Struble , two hard-hitting defencemen who will be tasked with regulating some of the shenanigans that inevitably take place whenever the Habs and Senators face off.

As for F. Xhekaj, his truculent approach is exactly what the Canadiens are looking for in their bottom-six, and though he's facing a crowded forward lineup, his intensity and affinity for providing more than just a physical presence should give him the inside track on any other young player in the mix. He will be playing in Montreal, on a fourth line alongside fellow prospects Owen Beck and Tyler Thorpe, the epitome of an energy line.

It should be noted that Ivan Demidov and Lane Hutson will not take part in either game, and will take the opportunity to rest prior to the start of the regular season on Tuesday, versus the Toronto Maple Leafs .

articles.title: Jenkins double gives Glens win over Carrick
articles.summary: A first-half Jordan Jenkins double gives Glentoran a 2-0 win over Carrick Rangers at the Oval.
articles.body:
A first-half Jordan Jenkins double proved enough to give Glentoran a 2-0 home win over Carrick Rangers.

The win is a second straight victory for interim manager Paddy McCourt since the recent departure of Declan Devine as Glens boss.

Both Jenkins' strikes came in an entertaining opening 45 minutes, with the game losing its fizz in the second period.

Carrick should have scored at least once as they went close on numerous occasions.

The game started in frenetic fashion with two big penalty shouts inside the opening five minutes.

Firstly, the visitors believed they should have had a spot-kick after Paul Heatley charged into the area and looked like he may have been caught by Glens' skipper Marcus Kane. Referee Tony Clarke put his whistle to his lips but then waved play on.

Then just seconds later at the other end it was the Glens turn to appeal for a spot-kick.

The ball was crossed from the left and it appeared to hit defender Kym Nelson on the arm after rebounding up from his leg. Protests rang around the ground, but Clarke remained unfazed once more.

Glentoran were rewarded on eight minutes though with the opening goal.

A long throw from Ryan Cooney on the right was headed on by Daniel Larmour. The ball fell kindly for Jenkins at the back post and he poked home from close range past Nathan Gartside in goal.

On 26 minutes it was number two for Glentoran and Jenkins.

Ross Clarke went on a mazy run through the Carrick defence before losing possession on the edge of the area. However, the ball rolled sidewards to Jenkins who curled home a fantastic right-footed effort that went high into the top right-hand corner of the goal giving Gartside no chance.

Six minutes later and the Glens almost grabbed a third as a scramble inside the box ended with Ross Clarke firing in an effort from close range, but Gartside was quick to react and dived low to parry the ball away.

Just a minute after the restart Carrick almost grabbed one back. Ben Buchanan-Rolleston provided a deflected cross in from the left that Andrew Mills should have claimed but instead he allowed it to bounce and it was flicked out towards the edge of the area where Heatley drove in a low effort that whistled just past the left upright.

Then just before the 70-minute mark Danny Gibson raced clear down the right for Rangers before he squared to Adam Lecky at the back post.

Lecky was no more than a yard out from goal but managed to strike the post when it appeared easier to score.

articles.summary: Luka Doncic is ready to take on a bigger leadership role for the Lakers.
articles.body:
As the Lakers move on from the franchise's LeBron James era , they understood many things would depart with the league's all-time leading scorer.

The biggest among them: the four-time league MVP's voice. And his leadership after achieving virtually every accolade in the NBA.

James' guidance, and his two-decades-plus of playing experience in the NBA, can't be replicated.

But the Lakers are ready for their current stars to step up as leaders in light of James' departure.

And Luka Doncic is ready to take that mantle as the Lakers fully entrench themselves in their next era.

If that wasn't already clear, Doncic made it evident during the Lakers' minicamp in his home country of Slovenia last month.

"Probably the leadership role," Doncic responded when asked what matters to him more now compared to five years ago toward the end of a 24-minute video posted on his YouTube page Friday about the camp in Slovenia.

Doncic added: "Trying to be a leader. Five years ago, I was [three years in] the league. I wasn't the leader I was supposed to [be]. So, leadership is an important part in my case now."

The Lakers already had an idea of what Doncic brought to the table in this regard since being traded to the franchise in February 2025.

Him treating his teammates to a Porsche Driving Experience in October 2025 during the preseason and surprising Lakers players, coaches and basketball operations staff with e-bikes as a Christmas present last year showcased his growth since arriving in Los Angeles .

But the Lakers got a closer look at what the team's leadership could look like moving forward with Doncic as the face of the franchise.

The Slovenian superstar organized a five-day trip for his teammates, which included a chartered flight, multiple dining experiences at Doncic's favorite restaurants, tours of the sights in Ljubljana (river cruise and Ljubljana Castle among them), golfing, rowing at Lake Bled and basketball activities.

His teammates raved about the experience.

To the point where they wrote Doncic handwritten notes to show him their appreciation for the experience.

"I'm definitely coming back," Collin Sexton said. "We had an amazing time. Great experience. Nothing but good vibes, nothing but love. Luka, man, appreciate you for bringing us out to your country and taking us back where it all started."

Leadership will be paramount for the Lakers moving forward.

James was among nine Lakers from the 2025-26 team who didn't return for this upcoming season.

Marcus Smart , Deandre Ayton , Rui Hachimura , Jaxson Hayes and Luke Kennard were among the other departures.

Doncic, Austin Reaves , Jarred Vanderbilt and Jake LaRavia are the only four players from last season's team who played at least 600 regular-season minutes that are returning for 2026-27.

Coach JJ Redick stressed the importance of connectedness during Thursday's joint availability with president of basketball operations/general manager Rob Pelinka.

In his eyes, the NBA's best teams over the last six to seven years have also been the most connected teams.

And because that isn't a coincidence, that'll be part of his messaging to the team throughout 2026-27 as Redick enters his third year as Lakers coach.

"There were times last year, there were times my first year where the team was connected," Redick said. "I really believe this group is gonna be connected from Day 1. And they already are."

And they are, in part, because of Doncic stepping up as a leader.

"There's a lot of new guys on the team," Doncic said. "Building chemistry is very important. That was the first thought, just to get the guys together. That's why I wanted to do it."

articles.title: ‘We Are Co-Creators’ — Rob Pelinka Reveals Luka Dončić’s Influence on Lakers’ Roster Decisions
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are entering a new era. Since LeBron James left Los Angeles for the Philadelphia 76ers, the team will no longer have the veteran super...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are entering a new era. Since LeBron James left Los Angeles for the Philadelphia 76ers , the team will no longer have the veteran superstar who has been at the center of the franchise for the last several years. Instead, much of the responsibility will now fall on Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves .

With the 2026-27 NBA season just weeks away, Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager Rob Pelinka has revealed more about Dončić's involvement in the team's direction.

Rob Pelinka's Recent Revelation Regarding Luka Dončić

In a recent interview with ESPN, Pelinka described Dončić as a highly creative basketball mind and a valued collaborator in decision-making.

While Pelinka remains the person with final authority over roster moves, Dončić has made it clear that he does not want to become the team's general manager or head coach. Instead, Pelinka described their relationship as a collaborative co-creator approach.

"I feel like we are co-creators with him, because he is a very creative basketball mind. Ultimately, I have the final responsibility to make calls on the roster, and Luka is very clear, like, 'I want you to do your job."

"I don't want to be the GM; I don't want to be the head coach. JJ, you are the coach; Rob, you are the GM and president. Do your jobs.' But we can co-create. Let's share ideas, let's break down pros and cons, and look at all aspects of a potential decision point before we make it," Pelinka said during the interview.

So, while Dončić indirectly made it clear that he does not want to be the GM, that does not mean he has a small role within the Lakers' organization. His role as a player is already massive.

During the 2025-26 NBA season, Dončić averaged 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds, 8.3 assists, 1.6 steals, and 0.5 blocks per game across 64 starts. He shot 47.6% from the field and 36.6% from three-point range while leading the league in scoring. Those numbers helped the Lakers finish the regular season with a 53-29 record.

Unfortunately for Los Angeles , Dončić's season ended earlier than expected after he suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury near the end of the regular season. Dončić ultimately missed the entire postseason while recovering from the Grade 2 left hamstring strain.

The Lakers still managed to get past the Houston Rockets 4-2 in the first round. However, their postseason run ended in the Western Conference semifinals, where the Oklahoma City Thunder swept them.

Now, with Dončić healthy again, expectations around the Lakers will be higher. The front office spent the offseason building a younger and deeper roster around him. Reaves was retained, while Walker Kessler was brought in as the team's new center.

The Lakers also added players such as Quentin Grimes , Collin Sexton , Matisse Thybulle , Ziaire Williams , Sandro Mamukelashvili , and Kevon Looney . So now, without LBJ, the Lakers are preparing for a season where Dončić will be the central figure both on the court and in the franchise's long-term plans.

articles.title: Deion Sanders weighs in on Jaguars’ usage of Travis Hunter
articles.summary: Deion Sanders says he won’t question Jacksonville from afar, but he knows exactly what former Colorado star Travis Hunter is capable of.
articles.body:
One of the biggest questions surrounding the Jacksonville Jaguars has been how two-way star Travis Hunter will be utilized. The Jaguars traded up to get him at No. 2 in the 2025 NFL Draft, but his promising rookie season came to a stop after he suffered a knee injury.

Hunter has seen limited snaps so far this season, which has led to some criticism. The latest example comes from Deion Sanders, who coached Hunter at both Jackson State and Colorado.

Through two games, Hunter has played 11 snaps on offense, according to PFF, with one reception, and 66 snaps on defense, as he shares playing time with Montaric Brown and Jarrian Jones . So far this season, his usage has been minimal, which Sanders questioned.

"I don't ask questions because I'm not there. I don't know what transpires. When we're not looking, I have no idea what's going on," he said on his CBS Colorado show, via Pro Football Talk . "I know who he was and who he is right now. I know what he's capable. I do know that."

Sanders previously criticized the Jaguars for not consulting with him on a strategy for how to get the most out of Hunter, though he said he has remained in touch with the Heisman Trophy winner.

It is yet to be seen if Hunter will see more playing time against the New England Patriots, but one suggested reason for his slow start is to ensure he remains healthy as he rebounds from last season's injury. According to an anonymous source , who spoke with The Athletic, this has been Jacksonville's plan all along, as he has played a total of just nine games in his entire NFL career, and the Jaguars hope to see him grow on both sides of the ball to have a long and productive career.

"He's been doing well," a second source told The Athletic's Jonathan Jones . "Obviously, still working back from not playing football for a long time. (I) think he's going to only keep getting better."

articles.title: Pittsburgh Pirates vs. Detroit Tigers: Justin Verlander’s last start
articles.summary: The Pirates are on the road looking to grab a win today.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Pirates vs. Detroit Tigers , September 26, 2026, 1:10 p.m. ET

The Pittsburgh Pirates are the answer to a unique baseball trivia question following today's game against the Detroit Tigers.

The Pirates will be the final team legendary pitcher Justin Verlander faces in his epic 21-year career that will almost certainly end with enshrinement into the Pro Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown once he is eligible.

Verlander began his career as the No. 2 overall pick in the 2004 MLB draft by the Detroit Tigers. He went on to make his MLB debut the following year, which led to an impressive 13-year run with the franchise. During that time, the Tigers qualified for the playoffs five times and the World Series twice, in 2006 and 2012.

With the Tigers exiting their contending window, Verlander was traded to the Houston Astros , who were poised to go on a dynastic run that saw them win the World Series in 2017 and 2022. After making appearances in the Fall Classic in 2019 and 2021, once he turned 40 years old, Verlander was on a quest to win 300 games, but he ultimately fell short of that goal.

Throughout his career, Verlander has a WAR of 82.3, with 266 wins to his name. But it's up to the Pirates to ensure he doesn't get No. 267.

articles.title: Mesa Mountain View stops 2-point try to seal 6A football win over Mesa
articles.summary: Mountain View held on for the win over Mesa as both teams were coming off tough losses last week looking to get on track.
articles.body:
The theme of for the game between Mesa Mountain View and Mesa on Friday, Sept. 25, was atonement.

Mesa (2-3) was looking to get back in the win column after suffering a 20-7 defeat on the road at Peoria Centennial Sept. 18, while Mountain View (3-2) was looking to bounce back from a heartbreaking 31-28 loss decided on a last-second field goal by Phoenix Brophy Prep.

In the end, it was Mountain View that got its atonement as it was able to stop a late two-point conversion attempt and come away with a 21-19 win and Mesa bragging rights over the rival Jackrabbits.

With Mountain View clinging to a 21-13 lead in the fourth quarter, Mesa attempted a comeback bid about half way through the quarter with a drive down the field. That drive was stopped cold with 6:39 left in regulation by a Toros interception. Mountain View was unable to extend its lead on its ensuing drive and gave Mesa one last chance to try to rally.

Senior quarterback Kane Anetema connected with senior Kingston Anetema on a 22-yard touchdown catch with just 28 seconds left in regulation to cut the Toros lead to 21-19, but Mesa's bid to tie the game failed when Kane Anetema's quarterback keeper on a 2-point try was stopped by the Toros' defense just shy of the goal line.

All three of the Toros' touchdowns came on the ground, courtesy of senior Coy Bodily's two-yard run with 9:11 left in the second quarter, sophomore Luke Whisenant's one-yard touchdown run later that quarter, and junior quarterback Brayden Merwin's one-yard run that proved to be the game-winning score with 2:02 left in the third quarter

Kane Anetema was the offensive star for the Jackrabbits, as all three of its touchdowns were via the air.

"We like that chip on our shoulder. You know, the Mountain View community likes that chip on our shoulder, and I'm really excited about going into our second half, getting in to region play, and going after that Brown Road trophy." - Mountain View head coach Andy Litten, on going into the second half of the season and what his team hopes to do the rest of the regular season

"We dominated the whole game. This is everything we said we were going to do. So, it's good to shut these guys up, finally." - Mountain View junior quarterback Brayden Merwin on beating rival Mesa.

Both teams will be in action Oct. 2, with Mountain View hosting Queen Creek and Mesa hosting Tucson Salpointe Catholic.
