articles.title: Jets vs. Lions: Bold predictions for Week 3 in Detroit
articles.summary: From a solid Geno Smith game to a dramatic finish in Detroit, here are five predictions for Sunday's matchup at Ford Field.
articles.body:
The New York Jets enter Week 3 with an opportunity to make a statement against the Detroit Lions .

Head coach Aaron Glenn returns to the Motor City for the first time as a head coach . The Jets defense enters the week ranked first in total yards allowed, and New York (1-1) is still searching for the offensive consistency needed to complement its strong defensive play.

Predicting NFL games is never easy, but that's what makes bold predictions fun.

Here are Jets Wire's five for Sunday's matchup as New York tries to improve to 2-1 :

Geno Smith posts a passer rating above 100

If there's a week for Geno Smith to deliver his most efficient performance of the season, this feels like it. Detroit's secondary has struggled through the first two weeks, and the Jets have enough weapons to take advantage if Smith gets adequate protection.

New York has moved the ball effectively at times this season but hasn't always finished drives or avoided costly mistakes. This week, Smith puts together a cleaner performance. He throws multiple touchdown passes, avoids turnovers, and finishes the afternoon with a passer rating north of 100.

Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both find the end zone

The Jets have made it clear they want a balanced offensive attack, and their backfield gives them the personnel to accomplish it. Hall remains one of the offense's most explosive players, while Allen has shown encouraging signs after a strong training camp and productive start to the season.

Detroit's defense will focus heavily on limiting New York's passing game, creating opportunities for the running backs to make an impact. By the end of the afternoon, both Hall and Allen have touchdown celebrations to their names.

The Jets hold Detroit under 200 total yards

This is where the predictions start getting truly bold. Detroit has plenty of offensive talent, and keeping any NFL team under 200 total yards is a difficult task. That said, the Jets have been dominant defensively through two weeks, ranking first in total defense and near the top of the league against both the run and the pass.

If Aaron Glenn's unit continues playing at its current level, it could turn in its most impressive performance of the season.

New York finally comes away with two interceptions

The prediction didn't work out last week , but there's no reason to abandon it now. The Jets have been around the football throughout the first two games. Defensive backs have gotten their hands on passes, pressure has forced hurried throws and the opportunities have been there.

The missing ingredient has been actually finishing the play. This week, that changes... for real this time. New York turns a pair of errant throws into interceptions and gives its offense valuable extra possessions.

Would it really be a bold predictions piece without forecasting a dramatic finish? The Lions are too talented to go away quietly, and the Jets haven't shown enough offensive consistency to suggest they'll comfortably pull away on the road. Expect a close game that remains undecided deep into the fourth quarter.

In the final minutes, New York's offense does just enough to move into scoring range. The Jets' kicker converts the game-winning field goal as time winds down, giving Glenn a memorable victory in his return to Detroit and sending New York home with its second win of the season.

articles.title: Tafuna scores hat-trick as USA edge Wales in WXV
articles.summary: Wales' resurgence suffers a blow with USA edging an entertaining WXV contest at Cardiff Arms Park.
articles.body:
Tries: Bevan, K Jones, Tuipulotu, Callender Cons: Bell 2

Tries: Tafuna 3, Coulibaly Cons: Vogel 3

Wales' resurgence suffered a disappointing blow with USA edging an entertaining WXV contest at Cardiff Arms Park.

Number eight Freda Tafuna, a standout player in USA's victory over Ireland last week, bagged a hat-trick of tries as the error-strewn hosts struggled to find the fluidity that saw them cruise past South Africa.

Erica Coulibaly also crossed for the visitors, while Wales stayed in the fight with scores from Keira Bevan, Kelsey Jones, Sisilia Tuipulotu and Alex Callender.

But the Eagles dominated the second-half, once again proving they are rising force in the women's game and living up to their status as a top-six side.

USA's winning streak now stretches to three games, while Wales must build again before they head to Japan next month.

Former Wales hooker Jonathan Humphreys on saw his USA's pack and its driving line-out provide the platform for the opening try, with Tafuna breaking through a determined defence.

Wales, meanwhile, struggled for a foothold with handling errors and indiscipline creeping into their game.

A knock-on led to Tafuna's second close-range effort and while Wales were offered a lifeline when replays showed Emily Henrich obstructed a defender, referee Amber McLachlan allowed it to stand.

Wales roared back to life with a clean line break from co-captain Kate Williams. Her namesake Amy then threatened down the wing before the ball was recycled back inside for Bevan, who did well to ride a tap tackle on her way to the line.

But Wales could not keep the momentum, a knock-on from the restart gifted USA back possession and once the ball found its way out to the pacy Coulibaly, there was little Wales could do to stop her.

Wales then had a shout of a yellow card for a high tackle on Tuipulotu, but were only given a penalty, which Lleucu George just about kicked to touch.

But there was no mistaking the quality of Wales' drive, with the pack powering hooker Jones to the line to get them back in the game.

Wales were finally able to hold onto the momentum and a penalty allowed the Welsh forwards to drive deep into USA territory and with the try-line begging, Tuipulotu bulldozed over for her third try in two games.

Freya Bell's conversion hit the post which looked to have given USA a two-point lead at the break, but that was until George put in a perfect grubber kick to peg the visitors back.

Wales won the turnover off line-out ball which Callender took quickly before finishing off the try, with Wales heading down the tunnel with the advantage.

Hopes of Wales pushing on after the break were quashed early on as the ever-clinical Tafuna powered over for her third of the afternoon.

It also gave the visitors a two-point lead which they never looked like surrendering in a one-sided half.

Starved of possession and territory, Wales were not helped by their set-piece, with both the scrum and line-out creaking.

The back line also struggled to get the ball through the hands despite the rallying cries from the lively 3,367 crowd.

Moments of inspiration were few and far between with a Kate Williams try-saving tackle and Callender turnover among the few bright moments.

It was a disappointing end to the first two games of Wales' campaign, while USA will march on with home games to come against Italy and world champions England.

articles.title: Steelers: Porter Jr.'s status doesn't look great amid back injury, trade rumors
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently navigating a complicated situation involving cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Initially listed with a “non-injury/conditionin...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently navigating a complicated situation involving cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Initially listed with a "non-injury/conditioning" tag, he returned to practice on a limited basis as the team prepared for their Week 3 divisional matchup against Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals .

While his presence on the practice field offered a glimmer of hope, the outlook for game day appears bleak. An illuminating report from Tom Pelissero on X indicated that Porter is unlikely to make his season debut on Sunday against the Bengals, although he is trending in the right direction to return soon. The report also noted that a trade is still a possibility amidst ongoing tensions.

Porter himself addressed this uncertainty when speaking with reporters on Thursday about stalled contract extension talks. He acknowledged to ESPN's Brooke Pryor that the failed negotiations are "old news" and stated that his primary focus is on getting back to full health. When asked if he expects to play at some point this season, he firmly responded, "Yeah, definitely." Still, whether that return will be with the Steelers or a new team via trade remains a significant storyline in the league.

As Pittsburgh prepares for kickoff at Acrisure Stadium, resolving the situation surrounding their star defensive back will be a top priority for the front office.

articles.title: LeBron James admits he is amazed by V.J. Edgecombe's overall talent and attitude
articles.summary: LeBron James is pleased to see how good V.J. Edgecombe has been so far.
articles.body:
Now that LeBron James is playing for the Philadelphia 76ers , he has a new set of teammates that he is getting to know. Among them is second-year standout V.J. Edgecombe , who has already impressed LeBron in the few weeks they've been teammates.

For a young player to impress James, it probably means that Edgecombe has done a lot of things that just tick all the boxes. He already showed that he was mature beyond his years during his rookie year, and it seems that has impressed James.

LeBron James loves what he has seen from V.J. Edgecombe so far

In his rookie season, Edgecombe averaged an impressive 16 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 4.2 assists per game. Considering he was not the star player, he already impressed during his first year in the league.

Now that he is playing with more stars, his numbers will probably dip. However, he will be learning from two Finals MVPs in LeBron and Jaylen Brown . In addition to that, he still has Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid to guide him too.

As the new leader of the 76ers , LeBron has already made connections with his new teammates. Edgecombe has already made a strong first impression, and that could go a long way when he is James' teammate moving forward.

"They say he was actually one of the leaders of the team as a 20-year-old rookie, and not in a disrespectful manner. It's not like he was just speaking just to be speaking or thinking he's better than this guy. No, it's just that they say he speaks with an intelligent confidence," James said about Edgecombe on the Mind the Game podcast .

"He's a guy that, you know, you got to put all the pieces together, but he's a guy that still has leaps to make, you know, with his athleticism, shot-making, defense."

James loves what he has seen from Edgecombe, and that is a big deal for the 76ers' future. There will come a time when Edgecombe is one of the franchise players, but since he is only in his second season, he will be a sponge who learns from his veteran teammates.

articles.title: Gloucester shock Exeter for superb victory
articles.summary: Gloucester produce an outstanding display in scoring seven tries to win 45-24 at last season's runners-up Exeter Chiefs.
articles.body:
Tries: Iosefa-Scott, E Roots, Varney, Gulley Cons: Slade 2

Tries: Loader 2, S Atkinson, Lake 2, Joseph, Denny Cons: C Atkinson 4, Barton

Gloucester delivered an outstanding performance on the first weekend of the new Prem season to stun Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park.

The Cherry and Whites only once won on the road last term as they finished eighth, but they matched that immediately with this superb showing.

Summer arrival, and new captain and Wales skipper, Dewi Lake led the way with two of their seven tries.

Winger Ben Loader helped himself to two, while Seb Atkinson, a fine solo effort from Will Joseph and a debut try from Junior Denny completed their try haul.

Exeter finished as runners-up last season after losing to Northampton Saints in the final in June, but they were well beaten.

Josh Iosefa-Scott and Ethan Roots grabbed their first-half scores before Stephen Varney and then Louie Gulley ensured they at least managed a bonus point.

After a few years in the doldrums, Exeter had a thrilling spring and summer with their unexpected run to The Prem final at Twickenham. With new American investment at Sandy Park, hopes are high about the direction of travel in Devon but this was a rude awakening to the new season for Rob Baxter's team.

The Cherry and Whites had a miserable campaign in limping home in eighth and they have not reached the play-offs for seven years, but the acquisition of Wales pair Lake and Jac Morgan has increased belief for the new campaign.

That was in evidence in their positive start as they worked the ball from one corner to the other, with Ben Redshaw's kick bouncing up perfectly for Loader to finish.

A sustained spell of phases eventually resulted in Iosefa-Scott driving over from close range for the hosts before a smart kick over the top from scrum-half Caolan Englefield allowed England centre Atkinson to win a foot race and touch down as Gloucester regained the lead.

Loader's second try extended that advantage as he showed impressive footwork to conjure up another fine kick towards the left corner and dive over.

Gloucester had produced an impressive opening half, but Roots grabbed a second try for the hosts as the flanker found himself on the wing with nobody able to stop his charge.

However, there was still time for the men from Kingsholm to secure a bonus point by the break as captain Lake brilliantly went over in the corner after he had turned down a kick at goal to earn a 26-12 interval lead

Lake's influence in his new team was there for all to see as he was at the back of a driving maul to grab his second try for a dominant Gloucester.

Joseph then scored the try of the game with a brilliant burst of speed from inside his own half that took him outside and inside three defenders.

Varney quickly grabbed Exeter's third try and with visiting flanker Freddie Thomas sin-binned for the final 10 minutes, replacement hooker Gulley went over on his Prem debut to ensure the Chiefs at least claimed a bonus point.

However, that debut try was matched by 18-year-old winger Denny, who scored with the last play of the game to seal Gloucester's first win in Devon since 2015.

articles.title: McGonigle strikes again as Limavady beat Cliftonville
articles.summary: Jamie McGonigle's fifth goal in three games was enough to secure a third win of the season for Limavady United as edge out Cliftonville at the Showgrounds.
articles.body:
Jamie McGonigle's fifth goal in three games was enough to secure a third win of the season for Limavady United as edged out Cliftonville at the Showgrounds.

The experienced frontman has been a revelation for the Roesiders since joining on loan from Coleraine before the transfer window shut at the start of the month.

McGonigle took advantage of a poor clearance by PJ Morrison to fire the hosts in front, but he could have had more as the Roesiders dominated the opening 45 minutes.

The Reds mustered a response after the break and ramped up the pressure in the closing stages with Dean McMaster going closest to an equaliser, but it wasn't to come as Jim Magilton's side slipped to a third defeat in-a-row

It was a fairly low-key opening quarter of an hour with Brian Healy's wayward effort from Rory Hale's pullback the closest either side came to threatening a goal.

Limavady United started to find their feet with the lively McGonigle causing problems on the counterattack.

After winning a corner on a break forward, Ruairi Boorman clipped the side netting from Danny Lafferty 's inswinging delivery.

McGonigle then dragged an effort across the face of goal from a Philip Lowry threaded pass on 18 minutes as the hosts continued to threaten.

Within a minute, the Coleraine loanee fired his side in front after Alfie Gaston forced Morrison into a poor clearance with McGonigle firing the ball over the keeper's head and into the net from 20 yards.

The Roesiders were full of confidence and were inches away from a second 10 minutes before the break as Gaston fizzed a low shot narrowly wide of the near post.

McGonigle then clipped the top of the crossbar with an audacious effort from out of the right-hand side on 38 minutes before Morrison palmed away a Ruairi Boorman header as the Roesiders came agonisingly close to a second goal before the break.

The 30-year-old continued to ask the questions after the break as he forced another good save out of Morrison on 56 minutes after a great turn in the box created the space for the striker to get his shot away.

Jim Magilton introduced Ben Quinn and Keevan Hawthorne in a bid to inject some attacking threat into his side and it almost had an instant reaction as teenage forward Hawthorne forced Marty Gallagher into his first meaningful action in the Limavady goal.

Gallagher was called into action again as we moved into the final 20 minutes. This time Dean McMaster let fly from 25-yards out with the Limavady stopper grabbing the ball at the second attempt after initially parrying the first shot.

McMaster tested Gallagher with another effort from outside the box on 80 minutes as the Reds continue to increase the pressure in search of an equaliser.

McClelland then looped a header onto the Roesiders crossbar from a Quinn corner with the defender having one more chance before the end, but his header was scooped up by Gallagher, much to the delight of the home support.
